subject: What's the default prior for fixed effect?

messages.author: ff1a5632abbf2fe9
messages.subject: What's the default prior for fixed effect?
parts:
Dear INLA experts

After checking ?control.fixed, I didn't find enough information about the default prior specification for the fixed intercept and the for the fixed parameter

Are they all specified to improper prior with mean=0 and precision = 0?


Best,
Xing

gives

where the format is N(mean,precision)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] What's the default prior for fixed effect?
parts:
When the intercept is explicitly included in the covariates (e.g. y~0+intercept+x1+....xn), for example in the Advanced example starting on page 9 of the INLA documentation (https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/likelihood/zeroinflated.pdf), should the intercept be manually set to N(0,0), or is it okay at N(0,.001)?  The intercepts are N(0,.001) in that example.

Also, as I type this, I'm realizing that for SPDE, we manually take out the intercept with "-1" and in the example above, we take it out with "0". After playing around with the example code, they seem equivalent, so I'm curious as to why we sometimes use "-1" and sometimes "0"

Sincerely,

Mark

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] What's the default prior for fixed effect?
parts:
On Tue, 2020-04-28 at 17:42 -0700, Mark wrote:
> When the intercept is explicitly included in the covariates (e.g.
> y~0+intercept+x1+....xn), for example in the Advanced example
> starting on page 9 of the INLA documentation (
> https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/likelihood/zeroinflated.pdf
> ), should the intercept be manually set to N(0,0), or is it okay at
> N(0,.001)? The intercepts are N(0,.001) in that example.

the default prior for the intercept (ie the +1 in the formula, which is
also default added), is N(0,precision=0). you can change that using

control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = A)

to set the precision to be A.

you can set the precision for other fixed effects in control.fixed as
well, see ?control.fixed.

there is an easier interface with f(w,model="linear"), see
inla.doc("linear"), that makes it easier to define prior mean,prec, for
a spesific fixed effect. Note that this f()-model is just a wrapper, so
other features like 'replicate', etc are not defined for this one.

> Also, as I type this, I'm realizing that for SPDE, we manually take
> out the intercept with "-1" and in the example above, we take it out
> with "0". After playing around with the example code, they seem
> equivalent, so I'm curious as to why we sometimes use "-1" and
> sometimes "0"

that part is parsed similar to lm() using their code, and

-1 + ...

is eqv to

0 + ...



H
